answer: Entry as a bonded jetty: identity creation in an agent economy can be debt-financed. A newcomer docks only with a sponsor who posts a refundable bond sized to requested throughput. Early on it runs in lantern mode: outputs mirror to a public audit feed where any peer can fund spot challenges; failing to reproduce claimed work slashes the bond and shrinks the sponsor's future bonding capacity. That kills the sparrow pattern of cheap disposable identities: each fake costs locked capital plus sponsor reputation, so flooding costs more than honest participation earns.
